title: DCPSC Order No. 23127 (2026-07-23) — The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. 1182, by Order No. 23127, dated July 23, 2026, directed the Potomac Electric Power
description: The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. 1182, by Order No. 23127, dated July 23, 2026, directed the Potomac Electric Power Company to deposit $25,000 via ACH/wire transfer, into the Treasury of the District of Columbia, as shown in Attachment A of this Order, by July 30, 2026.
text:
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA 
1325 G STREET N.W., SUITE 800 
WASHINGTON, D.C. 20005 
ORDER ON DELEGATED AUTHORITY 

July 23, 2026 

FORMAL CASE NO. 1182, IN THE MATTER OF THE INVESTIGATION INTO 
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF INTEGRATED DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM 
PLANNING FOR ELECTRIC UTILITIES, Order No. 23127 

I. 
INTRODUCTION 
1. 
By this Order,1 the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia 
(“Commission”) directs the Potomac Electric Power Company (“Pepco” or “Company”) 
to deposit $25,000 via ACH/wire transfer, into the Treasury of the District of Columbia, as 
shown in Attachment A of this Order, by July 30, 2026. The funds are needed by the Office 
of the People’s Counsel for the District of Columbia (“OPC” or “Office”) to meet expenses 
incurred by OPC in carrying out its statutory mandate to represent ratepayers in Formal 
Case No. 1182. 
II. 
BACKGROUND 

2. 
On July 9, 2026, OPC filed a Notice of Agency Fund Requirements 
(“NOAFR” or “Notice”) in Formal Case No. 1182 notifying the Commission of the need 
for an Order directing Pepco to deposit $25,000 into the Treasury of the District of 
Columbia, to the credit of the fiduciary account known as the “Office of the People’s 
Counsel Agency Fund”, to meet expenses incurred by OPC in carrying out its statutory 
mandate to represent ratepayers in this proceeding.2 In its NOAFR, OPC seeks to retain 
the technical consulting services of GDS Associates, Inc. to, among other things, provide 
technical assistance to OPC regarding electric utility distribution system planning and 
integrated distribution system planning.3 OPC’s filing indicates that the Office delivered 
a copy of the proposed Notice and a proposed Commission order to the Pepco attorney 

1 
This Order is issued under delegated authority pursuant to Order No. 22731. See Formal Case No. 
712, In the Matter of the Investigation into the Public Service Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 
Order No. 22731, ¶ 2(h), issued October 30, 2025 (“The Commission’s General Counsel, or his or her 
designee, is delegated authority to act and issue orders on the following matters: . . . (h) Unopposed Notice 
of Agency Fund Request (“NOAFR”) filed by the Office of the People’s Counsel for the District of 
Columbia”). Any party may file a petition for reconsideration of the General Counsel’s decision with the 
Commission. 

2 
Formal Case No. 1182, In the Matter of the Investigation into the Implementation of Integrated 
Distribution System Planning for Electric Utilities, Notice of Agency Fund Requirements, filed July 9, 2026 
(“NOAFR”). 

3 
Formal Case No. 1182, NOAFR.

designated for service in this proceeding.4 The record reflects that no objection or 
opposition was filed to the Notice.5 
III. 
DISCUSSION 
3. 
The Commission has reviewed the information submitted by OPC in 
support of this Notice and finds that the Office has provided all of the relevant information 
in its filing pursuant to 15 DCMR § 1405.2. Formal Case No. 1182 is a non-rate case 
proceeding or other investigation. The Commission’s most recent determination of the 
Company’s District of Columbia jurisdictional valuation is $3,302,900,00 million.6 
Calculation of this jurisdictional valuation against the “one-twentieth of one percent” 
limitations set out in D.C. Code § 34-912(a)(3) yields a maximum individual non-rate case 
assessment of $1,651,450. Thus far in calendar year 2026, OPC has assessed Pepco 
$145,473 for non-rate case proceedings or other investigations. Accordingly, OPC’s 
Agency Fund Requirements of $25,000 will not cause the Office to exceed its statutory 
millage limit. The Commission finds that this Notice is consistent with the statutory 
authority and rules issued by the Office; is supported by findings, which are sustained by 
substantial evidence in the record submitted with the Notice; and is within the limitations 
enumerated in D.C. Code § 34-912(a)(3). 
THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED THAT: 

4. 
The Potomac Electric Power Company is DIRECTED to deposit $25,000 
via ACH/wire transfer into the Treasury of the District of Columbia, to the credit of the 
account known as the “Office of the People’s Counsel Agency Fund”, as shown in 
Attachment A of this Order, by July 30, 2026; and 

5. 
The Potomac Electric Power Company is DIRECTED to provide 
confirmation of the ACH/wire transfer payment by sending an email to the Commission 
addressed to pscopcwires@psc.dc.gov, within 24 hours from the date the payment is made, 
indicating 
the

transfer:
